body.statement:
For every \(\beta>1/2\), with \(d=\lceil\beta\rceil+1\), there is a finite constant \(C_{\beta,\mathcal A}\), depending only on \(\beta\), \(\mathcal A\), and the fixed normalized order-\(d\) B-spline convention, such that the following holds.  If \(g\in H^\beta(\mathbb R)\) is supported on \(\mathcal A\), then, for every sufficiently large \(n\), there is a spline \(s_n\) in the span of \(\{\mathsf B_{k,K_n}:1\le k\le K_n+d\}\), extended by zero off \(\mathcal A\), for which
\[
 \|g-s_n\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}
 \le C_{\beta,\mathcal A}K_n^{1/2-\beta}
       \|g\|_{H^\beta(\mathbb R)}.
\]
The same constant works for all \(g\) in the stated Sobolev space; only finitely many one-sided boundary-stencil patterns occur.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a sufficiently large \(n\), put \(K=K_n\) and \(h=2B_A/K\), and let \(N_d\) be the cardinal B-spline of order \(d\), normalized so that its integer translates form a partition of unity.  We first construct a fixed local quasi-interpolant.  For every polynomial \(p\) of degree less than \(d\), the convolution identity \(N_d=N_{d-1}*\mathbf 1_{[0,1]}\), induction on \(d\), and the binomial formula show that
\[
 y\longmapsto \sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}k^rN_d(y-k),
 \qquad 0\le r<d,
\]
is a polynomial of degree \(r\) with leading coefficient one.  Thus the moment matrix taking the coefficients of a polynomial of degree less than \(d\) to these \(d\) discrete moments is triangular with unit diagonal.  Inverting this fixed matrix gives coefficient functionals \(\lambda_k\), each a fixed finite linear combination of point evaluations on a stencil of size depending only on \(d\), such that
\[
 Q_hg(x):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\lambda_k(g)N_d(x/h-k)
 \quad\text{satisfies}\quad Q_hp=p
 \quad\text{for every }p\in\mathbb P_{d-1}.                 \tag{1}
\]
At any fixed \(x\), only a number of terms depending on \(d\) is nonzero.  The inverse moment matrix is fixed, so there is \(C_d<\infty\) such that
\[
 |Q_hg(x)|\le C_d\max\{|g(v)|:|v-x|\le C_dh\}.              \tag{2}
\]
Apply (1)--(2) to \(e_\xi(v)=e^{i\xi v}\).  When \(|h\xi|\le1\), expand the exponential at \(x\) through degree \(d-1\).  The polynomial part cancels by (1), while the integral Taylor remainder is at most a constant times \(|h\xi|^d\) on every point in the fixed stencil.  When \(|h\xi|>1\), (2) and \(|e_\xi|=1\) give a constant bound.  Hence
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|e^{i\xi x}-Q_he_\xi(x)|
 \le C_d\min\{1,(h|\xi|)^d\}.                              \tag{3}
\]

Because \(\beta>1/2\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat g(\xi)|\,d\xi
 \le \|g\|_{H^\beta}
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}(1+\xi^2)^{-\beta}\,d\xi\right\}^{1/2}
 <\infty.                                                     \tag{4}
\]
Fourier inversion, the locality of \(Q_h\), and (4) permit termwise application of \(Q_h\).  Therefore (3) and Cauchy--Schwarz imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|g-Q_hg\|_\infty
 &\le C_d\int_{\mathbb R}
       \min\{1,(h|\xi|)^d\}|\widehat g(\xi)|\,d\xi\\
 &\le C_d\|g\|_{H^\beta}
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}\min\{1,(h|\xi|)^{2d}\}
                  (1+\xi^2)^{-\beta}\,d\xi\right\}^{1/2}.
                                                                  \tag{5}
 \end{aligned}
\]
For \(0<h\le1\), split the last integral at \(|\xi|=h^{-1}\).  Since \(d=\lceil\beta\rceil+1>\beta-1/2\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\int_{|\xi|\le h^{-1}}(h|\xi|)^{2d}(1+\xi^2)^{-\beta}\,d\xi
 \le C_{\beta,d}h^{2\beta-1},\\
 &\int_{|\xi|>h^{-1}}(1+\xi^2)^{-\beta}\,d\xi
 \le C_\beta h^{2\beta-1}.                                    \tag{6}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, on \(1\le|\xi|\le h^{-1}\) the first integrand is bounded by \(h^{2d}|\xi|^{2d-2\beta}\), whose integral is \(O(h^{2\beta-1})\); on \(|\xi|\le1\) it is \(O(h^{2d})=O(h^{2\beta-1})\), and the second line is the elementary tail integral, finite because \(\beta>1/2\).  Equations (5)--(6) give
\[
 \|g-Q_hg\|_\infty\le C_{\beta,d}h^{\beta-1/2}\|g\|_{H^\beta}.
                                                                  \tag{7}
\]

Extend \(g\) by zero off \(\mathcal A\), as it already is by the support premise, and restrict \(Q_hg\) to \(\mathcal A\).  This restriction is a spline of order \(d\) on the uniform partition.  Only the stencils meeting either endpoint differ from the interior translation pattern; there are at most \(2d\) such stencils and hence only finitely many boundary patterns.  Under the fixed clamped normalized basis convention, the restriction is in the span of \(\{\mathsf B_{k,K_n}:1\le k\le K_n+d\}\); extending that restriction by zero is exactly an admissible sieve spline.  Taking \(s_n=(Q_hg)|_{\mathcal A}\), substituting \(h=2B_A/K_n\) in (7), and absorbing \((2B_A)^{\beta-1/2}\) and the finitely many boundary constants into \(C_{\beta,\mathcal A}\) proves the assertion uniformly over \(g\).
